final_answer:
>>> The key to solving this problem is understanding the rate at which the machines work.  
>>> If 5 machines take 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, this implies that **each machine produces 1 widget in 5 minutes**. This is because all 5 machines are working simultaneously, so each contributes 1 widget to the total of 5 widgets in 5 minutes.  
>>> Therefore, the rate per machine is **1 widget per 5 minutes**, or **1/5 widgets per minute**.  
>>> When scaling up to 100 machines, the total production rate becomes **100 machines × (1/5 widgets per minute) = 20 widgets per minute**.  
>>> To produce 100 widgets at a rate of 20 widgets per minute, the time required is **100 widgets ÷ 20 widgets per minute = 5 minutes**.  
>>> This result makes sense because the number of machines and the number of widgets have increased proportionally (both multiplied by 20), so the time remains the same.  

**Answer:** It would take 5 minutes.
